cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before I book the trip, who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Whose objection would stop you paying the deposit?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's. But she's away, and her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the deputy release it alone, or does she still need the treasurer's permission?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 defers questions, but A5 neutral authority-chain probe does not maintain approval over B booking request.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 committee approval causes A3 veto question; B4 treasurer absence and deputy access cause A5 independent-release question, after an unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 urges timely booking and B4 supplies concrete payment authority information, credibly balancing progress and uncertainty.

heightening.evidence: B4 separates access from authority, and A5 probes which actually controls the deposit.

specificity.evidence: A1 trip booking, B2 coach deadline and B4 treasurer-deputy distinction establish the practical outcome.
